convertibility_reason: Uses only built-in iMA indicator. Simple crossover entry/exit on single timeframe. Percentage-based position sizing with loss-reduction logic. No external .mqh libraries for trading logic (Trade.mqh is standard MT5 include). Single position model.

other_exits: Position closed when opposite crossover signal occurs on same bar check

position_sizing.conditional_logic: Base lot = FreeMargin * MaximumRisk / margin_per_1lot. If consecutive losses exist (from deal history), lot is reduced by lot*losses/DecreaseFactor. Lot is then normalized to volume step and clamped to min/max volume.

custom_logic_notes: Entry signal uses bar[0] open and close crossing the MA (open on one side, close on the other). This is effectively a bar crossover of the MA line. The new-bar guard uses rt[1].tick_volume>1 check (only trades on first tick of new bar). Lot size decreases after consecutive losses using deal history scanning backwards until a profitable deal is found. PositionClose uses a deviation/slippage of 3 points.
python_conversion_notes: Straightforward conversion. The iMA handle maps to a standard SMA calculation. Entry logic is: if bar[0].open < MA and bar[0].close > MA then BUY; if bar[0].open > MA and bar[0].close < MA then SELL. New-bar guard requires tracking bar changes. Position sizing requires account balance/margin access and deal history iteration for consecutive loss counting. No SL/TP means positions are only closed on opposite signal. Trade.mqh is standard MT5 trade helper - in Python, use simple market order execution.
